title: Lockout/Tagout (Control of Hazardous Energy)
text:
[SOP-SAF-01: Lockout/Tagout (Control of Hazardous Energy)]
## Purpose
Prevent unexpected energization, start-up or release of stored energy while servicing machinery. Applies to every
machine in the plant: electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, gravitational, thermal, chemical and stored (accumulators, capacitors, springs, counterbalances).

title: Lockout/Tagout (Control of Hazardous Energy)
text:
[SOP-SAF-01: Lockout/Tagout (Control of Hazardous Energy)]
## Scope and authority
Only **Authorized Employees** (cert code LOTO) may apply locks. Affected employees (operators) must be notified. Contractors and vendor engineers must follow this procedure or be escorted by an authorized employee and apply their own personal lock.

title: Lockout/Tagout (Control of Hazardous Energy)
text:
[SOP-SAF-01: Lockout/Tagout (Control of Hazardous Energy)]
## Procedure
1. **Prepare.** Identify all energy sources on the machine energy-source card (posted at each machine). Review the machine-specific lockout procedure. Collect locks, tags and a multi-lock hasp.
2. **Notify.** Tell the Line Lead and operator(s) that the machine will be locked out and why. Press the area Andon so production is aware.
3. **Shut down** the machine using the normal stop sequence (do not use E-stop as a stop).
4. **Isolate.** Open and lock each energy-isolating device: main disconnect, hydraulic pump motor starter, pneumatic dump valve, and individual shutoff valves. For robots, lock the controller main switch and the cell mains disconnect.
5. **Apply locks and tags.** Each authorized person applies a personal lock and a tag with name, date and shift. One person = one lock.
6. **Release stored energy.** Bleed hydraulic accumulators via the manual dump valve, vent pneumatics, block or lower suspended loads (die, cushion, robot arm on its mechanical stops), discharge capacitors/drives (wait for DC link discharge time on the drive label, minimum 5 minutes for servo amplifiers).
7. **Verify zero energy (Try-out).** Attempt a start from the HMI/control panel and confirm nothing moves. Verify electrical zero energy with a rated meter (live-dead-live) where exposed conductors are involved. Return controls to OFF.
8. **Perform the work.** If a lock-holder leaves the work, their lock stays on. Shift change: use the group lockout board and handover per SOP-MNT-03.
9. **Release.** Clear tools and people, reinstall guards, remove locks (each person removes their own), notify affected employees, re-energize, and run a test cycle with the operator.

title: Lockout/Tagout (Control of Hazardous Energy)
text:
[SOP-SAF-01: Lockout/Tagout (Control of Hazardous Energy)]
## Special cases
- **Hydraulic presses / Giga Press:** accumulator pre-charge gas (nitrogen) is stored energy: use the accumulator dump valve and confirm gauge reads zero before any hose or valve work. Die must be blocked with the safety blocks when working between platens.
- **Robot cells:** lock out controller and the weld transformer/servo gun supply; the arm can drop when brakes release; use mechanical stops/blocking for axes 2 and 3.
- **HV battery equipment:** follow SOP-SAF-02 in addition to this procedure.

title: Lockout/Tagout (Control of Hazardous Energy)
text:
[SOP-SAF-01: Lockout/Tagout (Control of Hazardous Energy)]
## Lock removal when the owner is unavailable
Only the Maintenance Manager (or delegate) after documented attempt to contact the owner, a physical check of the machine, and notification of the employee upon return.

title: Lockout/Tagout (Control of Hazardous Energy)
text:
[SOP-SAF-01: Lockout/Tagout (Control of Hazardous Energy)]
## Records
LOTO permit stored in CMMS attached to the work order. Annual periodic inspection by EHS for each machine-specific procedure.

title: High-Voltage (EV Battery) Safe Work Procedure
text:
[SOP-SAF-02: High-Voltage (EV Battery) Safe Work Procedure]
## Purpose
Control electrical shock, arc-flash and thermal risks when working on EV battery modules, packs and HV test equipment (typically 400 V to 800 V nominal; a pack with ~198 cells in series can operate from roughly 610 to 835 V).

title: High-Voltage (EV Battery) Safe Work Procedure
text:
[SOP-SAF-02: High-Voltage (EV Battery) Safe Work Procedure]
## Qualification
- **NFPA 70E qualified person (cert HV):** may work on or near exposed energized parts only with an approved energized work permit.
- **HVB (non-electrical HV awareness):** may handle sealed, isolated packs and use galvanically isolated fastening tools; may not open HV enclosures.

title: High-Voltage (EV Battery) Safe Work Procedure
text:
[SOP-SAF-02: High-Voltage (EV Battery) Safe Work Procedure]
## Rules
1. Treat every pack as energized. A pack is NOT safe until the **service disconnect** is pulled, the pack is verified at zero volts with a CAT III/IV rated meter on both poles to chassis, and the insulation resistance measurement is recorded.
2. PPE for qualified persons: Class 0 (1000 V) rubber insulating gloves with leather protectors (air-tested before shift), arc-rated face shield and clothing, insulated tools (1000 V rated). Non-qualified persons wear cut-resistant gloves and safety glasses and keep a 1 m exclusion distance from open HV.
3. Fastening tools used near HV busbars must have **galvanically isolated chucks**; never substitute a standard bit or socket.
4. Remove all metal jewelry. No conductive tools on top of open packs. Use dissipative mats.
5. Two-person rule for all HV work; one is the safety observer with the E-stop in hand and trained in rescue (non-conductive hook).
6. Cells outside spec (swelling, odor, leakage, surface temperature > 60 C): STOP, move people out, follow SOP-SAF-03.

title: High-Voltage (EV Battery) Safe Work Procedure
text:
[SOP-SAF-02: High-Voltage (EV Battery) Safe Work Procedure]
## HV test equipment (pack EOL, HV tester)
- Verify interlock loop and warning beacons each shift (daily check PM-BE).
- Discharge and verify zero before connecting/disconnecting leads. Insulation test voltage is applied only when cell door is closed and interlock confirmed.
- A **HV insulation fault** alarm (TST-HV-ISO) stops the test; do not retry more than once without a qualified person inspecting cables for moisture or damage.

title: High-Voltage (EV Battery) Safe Work Procedure
text:
[SOP-SAF-02: High-Voltage (EV Battery) Safe Work Procedure]
## Escalation
Any HV incident or suspected fault is **Level 6 immediately**: page HV Safety Engineer and EHS. Quarantine the pack in the marked battery quarantine bay (outdoors cage, 3 m separation).

title: High-Voltage (EV Battery) Safe Work Procedure
text:
[SOP-SAF-02: High-Voltage (EV Battery) Safe Work Procedure]
## Records
Energized work permits, insulation resistance logs, PPE glove test log, and incident reports.

title: Battery Thermal Event & Fire Emergency Response
text:
[SOP-SAF-03: Battery Thermal Event & Fire Emergency Response]
## Purpose
Respond safely to cell venting, smoke, swelling, fire or thermal runaway of battery cells, modules or packs.

title: Battery Thermal Event & Fire Emergency Response
text:
[SOP-SAF-03: Battery Thermal Event & Fire Emergency Response]
## Recognition
Hissing/venting, white or grey smoke, sweet solvent odor, unexpected heat, swelling, voltage collapse flagged by the test system, or flames.

title: Battery Thermal Event & Fire Emergency Response
text:
[SOP-SAF-03: Battery Thermal Event & Fire Emergency Response]
## Immediate actions (first 60 seconds)
1. **Alarm and evacuate**: hit the nearest fire pull station and shout "battery fire". Evacuate everyone at least 15 m upwind; do not fight a pack fire beyond incipient stage.
2. Cut power to the station using the E-stop if it is safe to do so.
3. Call the on-site emergency team (radio channel EMERG) and 911 from the control room.
4. Page EHS and the HV Safety Engineer (Level 6).

title: Battery Thermal Event & Fire Emergency Response
text:
[SOP-SAF-03: Battery Thermal Event & Fire Emergency Response]
## If incipient (a single cell venting, no flame)
Trained responders may isolate by moving the module using insulated tools into the quarantine cage if the surface temperature is below 80 C. Otherwise wait for fire service.

title: Battery Thermal Event & Fire Emergency Response
text:
[SOP-SAF-03: Battery Thermal Event & Fire Emergency Response]
## Fire suppression notes
Large volumes of water are the recommended agent for lithium-ion fire cooling when applied by fire service; Class D and dry chemical agents are not effective on thermal runaway. The plant's sprinkler system covers the battery bay.

title: Battery Thermal Event & Fire Emergency Response
text:
[SOP-SAF-03: Battery Thermal Event & Fire Emergency Response]
## After the event
Keep the area closed for at least 24 h. Monitor surface temperature of nearby packs with the thermal camera for re-ignition. Preserve evidence. Notify Quality and file an incident report. A Level 6 RCA is required.

title: Robot Cell Entry, Teaching and Safeguarding
text:
[SOP-SAF-04: Robot Cell Entry, Teaching and Safeguarding]
## Purpose
Protect personnel who enter robot cells for maintenance, teaching or troubleshooting. Applies to all FANUC, KUKA, ABB, Duerr and cobot cells.

title: Robot Cell Entry, Teaching and Safeguarding
text:
[SOP-SAF-04: Robot Cell Entry, Teaching and Safeguarding]
## Safeguards
Fence with interlocked gate, trapped-key or safety-rated door switch, light curtains at material windows, safety scanners at open cells, E-stops on each operator station and on the teach pendant. Safety circuit validation is part of the annual PM (ISO 10218 requires verification at defined intervals).

title: Robot Cell Entry, Teaching and Safeguarding
text:
[SOP-SAF-04: Robot Cell Entry, Teaching and Safeguarding]
## Entry procedure
1. Request entry through the cell operator; stop the cell in a safe state (arm at home).
2. Switch the controller to **T1 (manual reduced speed)**. Take the teach pendant with you and keep the enabling (deadman) switch accessible.
3. If work is not required with power on, **lock out** per SOP-SAF-01. For work inside the envelope with robot power ON (teaching, collision recovery), only a trained person may enter and must carry the pendant; nobody else may operate the cell controls (use the trapped key / personal lock on the gate).
4. Never rely on a stopped robot: stored program waits, servo-gun closes and weld current can start unexpectedly. Check the position of other robots in a shared cell.
5. Leaving: remove all tools and personal items, close and lock the gate, reset the safety circuit, check that people are clear, restore AUTO mode only from outside the fence.

title: Robot Cell Entry, Teaching and Safeguarding
text:
[SOP-SAF-04: Robot Cell Entry, Teaching and Safeguarding]
## Typical alarms seen on entry
- SRVO-007 (external E-stop) / KSS emergency stop active: identify which device opened the chain before resetting.
- SRVO-230 chain abnormal: do not bypass; call controls.

title: Robot Cell Entry, Teaching and Safeguarding
text:
[SOP-SAF-04: Robot Cell Entry, Teaching and Safeguarding]
## Records
Entries logged on the cell entry sheet; teach changes logged per SOP-MNT-06.

title: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol
text:
[SOP-MNT-01: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol]
## Purpose
Ensure the right person is engaged at the right time when equipment faults, defining who to page, when, and how quickly they must acknowledge.

title: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol
text:
[SOP-MNT-01: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol]
## Roles
- **Operator:** first responder. Pull the Andon, note time and fault code, tell the Line Lead.
- **Line Lead (L0):** confirms the stop, tries a safe reset (once), calls the on-shift Primary Technician for the machine (radio channel MAINT or pager).
- **L1 Primary Technician:** the on-shift technician assigned to the machine in the trade matching the fault (mechanical, electrical, hydraulics, robotics, controls, process).
- **L2 Backup Technician:** same trade, same shift; paged if no ack within 5 minutes or if a second person is required (two-person work).
- **L3 Maintenance Supervisor (shift):** for the zone; paged on thresholds below, any severity-3+ fault, or any safety concern.
- **L4 Area Engineer (on-call):** reliability, controls or process engineer for the area, selected by fault trade.
- **L5 Vendor support:** OEM emergency line per machine (see machine record for contract and SLA).
- **L6 Plant management:** Maintenance Manager, Operations Director, Plant Manager; always engaged immediately for safety events.

title: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol
text:
[SOP-MNT-01: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol]
## Escalation timers (minutes of line-impacting downtime)
| Machine criticality | L1 tech | L2 backup | L3 supervisor | L4 engineer | L5 vendor | L6 plant mgmt |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (line-stopping) | 2 | 8 | 15 | 30 | 90 | 180 |
| B (buffered) | 5 | 15 | 30 | 60 | 180 | 360 |
| C (non-critical) | 10 | 30 | 60 | 120 | 360 | 720 |

Timers run from the Andon. A repeat of the same fault within 24 hours moves the escalation straight to L4.

title: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol
text:
[SOP-MNT-01: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol]
## Acknowledgement
Pages must be acknowledged within 3 minutes (A), 5 minutes (B), 10 minutes (C). If no ack, the sender pages the next level and calls the radio/phone. The Maintenance Supervisor can reassign technicians across trades.

title: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol
text:
[SOP-MNT-01: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol]
## Fault-trade routing
- Robot alarm (SRVO-/KSS-/ABB-): ROBO tech; controls engineer for DCS/safety parameter issues.
- Hydraulic pressure/temperature/leak: HYD tech.
- Drive overload, breakers, motors: ELEC tech.
- PLC/MES comms, AGV navigation: CTRL tech.
- Torque NOK, calibration, process drift, laser power: PROC tech with process engineer.
- Mechanical wear/jam: MECH tech.

title: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol
text:
[SOP-MNT-01: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol]
## Safety overrides
Injury, fire/smoke, HV event, paint Ex-purge fault, molten metal or die water leak: **Level 6 immediately**, follow SOP-SAF-03 / SOP-CAS-02 / SOP-PNT-01.

title: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol
text:
[SOP-MNT-01: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol]
## Communication
Use the area channel for status every 15 minutes during Level 3+ events. The Maintenance Supervisor posts the event summary into the shift handover (SOP-MNT-03). After vendor engagement the Planner opens a service ticket in CMMS.

title: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol
text:
[SOP-MNT-01: Fault Escalation and Paging Protocol]
## Who to page when information is incomplete
Page the **Maintenance Supervisor** for the zone; they know the on-call rota. The on-call rota (weekly) lists primary and secondary engineers per discipline.

title: Work Order Management, Priorities and Failure Coding
text:
[SOP-MNT-02: Work Order Management, Priorities and Failure Coding]
## Priority definitions
- **P1 (emergency):** safety risk or line stop at a criticality-A machine, response immediately.
- **P2 (urgent):** major fault or risk of line stop within the shift, response < 30 min.
- **P3 (normal):** degraded operation, planned PM, inspections; scheduled within 7 days.
- **P4 (minor):** nuisance faults and improvements; scheduled within 30 days.

title: Work Order Management, Priorities and Failure Coding
text:
[SOP-MNT-02: Work Order Management, Priorities and Failure Coding]
## Closure requirements (CM work orders)
Technician must record: fault code, symptom, diagnosis, action taken, root cause (free text) and category, parts used with part numbers, downtime minutes, and any follow-up needed. For P1/P2 events with downtime above 4 hours an RCA is raised within 3 days.

title: Work Order Management, Priorities and Failure Coding
text:
[SOP-MNT-02: Work Order Management, Priorities and Failure Coding]
## Root-cause categories
Wear/aging, Lubrication, Contamination, Electrical/instrumentation, Operator/material handling, Software/configuration, Thermal/cooling, Leak/sealing, Process drift, Unknown. "Unknown" must be re-reviewed by the area engineer within 7 days.

title: Work Order Management, Priorities and Failure Coding
text:
[SOP-MNT-02: Work Order Management, Priorities and Failure Coding]
## PM execution
PM work orders are generated by interval (operating hours, from machine runtime counters, or calendar days). Technicians complete the checklist, record findings and close. Deferred PMs require supervisor approval and rescheduling within 14 days. PMs more than 14 days overdue on criticality-A machines are escalated to the Maintenance Manager.

title: Work Order Management, Priorities and Failure Coding
text:
[SOP-MNT-02: Work Order Management, Priorities and Failure Coding]
## Repeat failures
Same machine and fault code within 14 days triggers an automatic review (4M: man, machine, method, material). Three occurrences in 90 days opens a reliability project.

title: Condition Monitoring, Oil Analysis and Alert Thresholds
text:
[SOP-MNT-05: Condition Monitoring, Oil Analysis and Alert Thresholds]
## Purpose
Detect developing failures from sensor trends, oil analysis and thermography so work is planned before breakdown.

title: Condition Monitoring, Oil Analysis and Alert Thresholds
text:
[SOP-MNT-05: Condition Monitoring, Oil Analysis and Alert Thresholds]
## Sensors and thresholds
Each machine publishes channels (vibration mm/s RMS, motor current A, motor temperature C, hydraulic pressure bar, oil temperature C, filter differential pressure bar, battery voltage V, laser power %, etc.). Each channel has a **nominal**, **warn** and **alarm** value defined in the machine record. Actions:
- **Warn:** raise a PdM work order, inspect within 5 working days, increase sampling frequency.
- **Alarm:** treat as imminent failure; supervisor decides whether to continue production using SOP-OPS-02 (run-extension decisions).
- Trends crossing 70% of the nominal-to-warn distance for more than 7 days also trigger a PdM work order.

title: Condition Monitoring, Oil Analysis and Alert Thresholds
text:
[SOP-MNT-05: Condition Monitoring, Oil Analysis and Alert Thresholds]
## Oil analysis
- Gearbox and hydraulic oil sampled quarterly (robot gearboxes at annual PM).
- Iron (Fe) > 200 ppm triggers a work order for oil change and internal inspection.
- Hydraulic fluid cleanliness target ISO 4406 18/16/13 for servo valves (17/15/12 for presses with proportional valves); particle count above target triggers filtration/flush.
- Water > 0.1% in hydraulic oil triggers cooler leak check.

title: Condition Monitoring, Oil Analysis and Alert Thresholds
text:
[SOP-MNT-05: Condition Monitoring, Oil Analysis and Alert Thresholds]
## Thermography
Quarterly on switchgear, VFDs, motor terminal boxes and compressor motors. Hot spots > 15 C over reference or > 40 C over ambient raise a P2 work order.

title: Condition Monitoring, Oil Analysis and Alert Thresholds
text:
[SOP-MNT-05: Condition Monitoring, Oil Analysis and Alert Thresholds]
## Anomaly detection
The plant's anomaly detection model (shared with the digital twin) scores sensor windows and attaches SHAP feature contributions to alerts. Engineers review alerts daily; confirmed true positives are logged as PdM work orders and used to retrain the model.

title: Management of Change and Robot Program Backup
text:
[SOP-MNT-06: Management of Change and Robot Program Backup]
## Rules
1. All robot, PLC, CNC and test-system programs are backed up to the plant version control server **before and after** any change. Robots: full controller backup (all programs, system variables, DCS/safety parameters, mastering data).
2. Changes to safety parameters (FANUC DCS, KUKA SafeOperation, ABB SafeMove) require controls engineer approval and a documented safety verification report.
3. After any mastering/calibration event: validate TCP, run the accuracy check and record results.
4. Firmware updates only during planned downtime with vendor support and rollback plan.
5. A DCS checksum mismatch alarm (e.g. SRVO-402) after a program change must be resolved by re-applying approved parameters, not by editing the checksum.

title: General Robot Alarm Recovery
text:
[SOP-ROB-01: General Robot Alarm Recovery]
## Steps
1. Read the alarm on the pendant and note code, axis/group, and time. Take a photo of the alarm history.
2. If the alarm is safety related (E-stop, chain abnormal, DCS), identify and fix the cause before reset; never bypass interlocks.
3. If the robot stopped mid-process (weld, glue, paint), check part status and quarantine suspect parts.
4. **Collision / disturbance alarms (e.g. SRVO-050, ABB 50026):** enter the cell per SOP-SAF-04, jog the robot clear in T1 using the collision release, inspect tool, fixture, and part for damage, check payload settings, and look for reducer wear if the alarm repeats on the same axis (rising motor current on J2/J3 is an early sign).
5. **Overtemperature / OVC alarms:** let the motor cool, check duty cycle, cooling surfaces and cabinet fans.
6. **Brake alarms:** run the brake test; failure means stop the robot and call the robotics supervisor (axis may drop).
7. After repair, run the program at reduced override, then full speed with an empty cell, and finally in production with first-part inspection.

title: FANUC Backup Battery Alarms (SRVO-062 BZAL / SRVO-065 BLAL) and Re-mastering
text:
[SOP-ROB-02: FANUC Backup Battery Alarms (SRVO-062 BZAL / SRVO-065 BLAL) and Re-mastering]
## Background
FANUC controllers keep absolute position (mastering) data in pulse coders powered by backup batteries. Two alarms matter:
- **SRVO-065 BLAL:** battery voltage is low, data is still intact. Warning, replace soon.
- **SRVO-062 BZAL:** battery voltage is zero, encoder data lost. Critical, the axis must be re-mastered.

Batteries (lithium A02B-0200-K102 in the controller and robot base on many models) typically last 1-2 years. Replace on a schedule or at the first BLAL.

title: FANUC Backup Battery Alarms (SRVO-062 BZAL / SRVO-065 BLAL) and Re-mastering
text:
[SOP-ROB-02: FANUC Backup Battery Alarms (SRVO-062 BZAL / SRVO-065 BLAL) and Re-mastering]
## SRVO-065 BLAL (low battery) - do this the same shift
1. Keep the controller **powered ON** during replacement so data stays alive.
2. Replace the controller battery and the robot-base battery one at a time, checking polarity.
3. Record the date on the robot tag; clear the alarm.

title: FANUC Backup Battery Alarms (SRVO-062 BZAL / SRVO-065 BLAL) and Re-mastering
text:
[SOP-ROB-02: FANUC Backup Battery Alarms (SRVO-062 BZAL / SRVO-065 BLAL) and Re-mastering]
## SRVO-062 BZAL (battery dead) - re-mastering
1. Replace batteries (check polarity and connector contact; verify the battery cable inside the base is not unplugged or broken).
2. On the pendant, clear the pulse coder alarm with **RES_PCA** (position capture reset) and power cycle (FCTN > 0 > 8 or controller restart).
3. Set **$MASTER_ENB = 1** and select Master/Cal, in T1 mode.
4. Jog the robot to the zero position by the **witness marks** (or use the calibration fixture/quick-master reference stored in the last backup).
5. Master (zero position master) all affected axes, then Calibrate. Cycle power.
6. Verify the zero position and TCP; run the weld/path accuracy check and obtain controls/robotics sign-off. If it still fails after battery replacement check battery installation polarity, contact cleanliness, and the encoder or cable (FANUC service).

title: FANUC Backup Battery Alarms (SRVO-062 BZAL / SRVO-065 BLAL) and Re-mastering
text:
[SOP-ROB-02: FANUC Backup Battery Alarms (SRVO-062 BZAL / SRVO-065 BLAL) and Re-mastering]
## Notes
Typical downtime for BZAL is 90-300 minutes. Keep a controller backup current so that mastering data can be compared to the backup (positional accuracy is lost if the physical position differs from the backed-up mastering).

title: KUKA Maintenance Reminders and Gear Oil Change
text:
[SOP-ROB-03: KUKA Maintenance Reminders and Gear Oil Change]
## Background
KUKA KRC4/KR C5 controllers raise maintenance reminder messages based on operating hours or calendar time. Typical OEM intervals: gearbox oil replacement every 10,000-20,000 hours or 3-4 years for main axes (A1-A3), inline-wrist belt inspection/tension at 8,000-10,000 h (6-axis inline wrist only), electrical cabinet inspection by calendar. Newer KR QUANTEC PA palletizers specify an oil change at 20,000 operating hours; some models list "20,000 hourly / 5 yearly gear oil change".
Approved lubricant: KUKA-approved synthetic gear oil, ISO VG 150 (for example Shell Tivela S150 on QUANTEC primary axes; about 8 L per primary axis, confirm the exact quantity in the model manual).

title: KUKA Maintenance Reminders and Gear Oil Change
text:
[SOP-ROB-03: KUKA Maintenance Reminders and Gear Oil Change]
## Oil change procedure (summary)
1. **Burn hazard:** if the robot has just stopped, oil and surfaces may be very hot. Let it cool to a safe temperature but drain while still warm for best flow.
2. Lock out the robot (SOP-SAF-01) and block axis 2/3 against falling.
3. Pull out the oil drain hose; place a suitable receptacle under it; unscrew the union nut of the drain hose.
4. Drain completely; inspect the drained oil for metal particles (indicator of internal wear); photograph and record.
5. Refit the hose, refill through the filler port with approved oil to the level mark, replace sealing washers.
6. Run the robot through the warm-up program (axes 1-3 at 50% for 15 minutes), re-check level and leaks.
7. **Reset the maintenance counter** from the SmartPAD (Maintenance > Resets) and record the service date and hours on the WO.

title: KUKA Maintenance Reminders and Gear Oil Change
text:
[SOP-ROB-03: KUKA Maintenance Reminders and Gear Oil Change]
## Related checks
Inspect robot arm housing for oil leakage at the gearbox seals (A1-A3 primary, A4-A6 secondary). A leak that returns within one shift indicates seal wear or an over-filled/blocked-vent gearbox. Brake test on all axes after oil changes.

title: Spot Weld Tip Dressing, Weld Quality Verification and Weld Gun Care
text:
[SOP-ROB-04: Spot Weld Tip Dressing, Weld Quality Verification and Weld Gun Care]
## Tip care
- Dress or change electrode caps at the programmed stepper count (typically every 16-100 welds depending on coating and schedule).
- Cooling water flow at each gun must be at least 4 l/min; low flow causes tip overheating and sticking (fault codes WG-TIP-WEAR, KSS-SPOT-STICK).
- If a tip sticks (robot motion blocked), break the tip free using the manual release, replace the cap, and check the weld schedule and flow before resuming.

title: Spot Weld Tip Dressing, Weld Quality Verification and Weld Gun Care
text:
[SOP-ROB-04: Spot Weld Tip Dressing, Weld Quality Verification and Weld Gun Care]
## Verification
- Peel test (chisel/destructive) at start of each shift per weld group; nugget diameter at least 4 x sqrt(t) where t is thinnest sheet thickness.
- Ultrasonic nugget testing for critical structural welds weekly.
- Any gun with low-current alerts (weld current falling below warn) is inspected for cable/shunt wear and transformer cooling.

title: Spot Weld Tip Dressing, Weld Quality Verification and Weld Gun Care
text:
[SOP-ROB-04: Spot Weld Tip Dressing, Weld Quality Verification and Weld Gun Care]
## Weld transformer overtemperature (WG-TRANSF-TEMP)
Check coolant flow and temperature; verify duty cycle; check thermal switch; do not defeat the switch. Replace the transformer if windings are suspect.

title: Giga Press Start-up, Shutdown and Daily Hydraulic Checks
text:
[SOP-CAS-01: Giga Press Start-up, Shutdown and Daily Hydraulic Checks]
## Machine overview
IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 class: 6,100 t (about 60,000 kN) clamping force, die height 2,400 mm, ~430 t, with accumulator-based injection (fill time roughly 120 ms for a 6,000 t class machine), Block-Control tie-bar monitoring with automatic clamping-force adjustment, automatic toggle lubrication and servo-driven guarding.

title: Giga Press Start-up, Shutdown and Daily Hydraulic Checks
text:
[SOP-CAS-01: Giga Press Start-up, Shutdown and Daily Hydraulic Checks]
## Start-up
1. Verify LOTO released and the machine area clear. Check the die is locked and cooling circuits are connected.
2. Hydraulic walk-down: reservoir level at least 85%, oil temperature between 35 and 50 C, no leaks, filter dP indicators green, accumulator pre-charge gauges within the setpoint on the machine card.
3. Start hydraulic pumps, wait for pressure to stabilize at setpoint (nominal ~280 bar on the main circuit). If pressure fails to build or is more than 10% low, stop (fault GP-PRESS-LOW).
4. Warm up die with the die thermal control units to the die temperature recipe before first shot. Run 3 dry cycles and check clamping force distribution across the four tie bars; investigate a deviation > 3% (fault GP-TIEBAR, run tie-bar calibration).
5. Start the dosing furnace transfer and inject the first shots at reduced speed; verify fill time and shot curve against the golden profile before full speed.

title: Giga Press Start-up, Shutdown and Daily Hydraulic Checks
text:
[SOP-CAS-01: Giga Press Start-up, Shutdown and Daily Hydraulic Checks]
## During production
- Check the shot profile each shift: a slow fill or low accumulator recovery points to accumulator pre-charge loss, valve response issues or sleeve wear (GP-SHOT-SLOW).
- Record hydraulic temperature; above 58 C is a warn. Clean oil cooler and check water flow; above 65 C is an alarm: stop at end of shot.
- Trim, X-ray and machining cells downstream depend on this machine (criticality A).

title: Giga Press Start-up, Shutdown and Daily Hydraulic Checks
text:
[SOP-CAS-01: Giga Press Start-up, Shutdown and Daily Hydraulic Checks]
## Shutdown
Run last shot, retract plunger, close die with low force, switch off pumps, vent accumulators only for maintenance (LOTO). Record the shot counter and any parameter changes.

title: Die Change and Die Cooling Leak / Molten Metal Safety
text:
[SOP-CAS-02: Die Change and Die Cooling Leak / Molten Metal Safety]
## Die change
1. Cool the die to the permitted handling temperature; remove die spray and cooling hoses.
2. LOTO the press and apply the die-safety blocks between platens (SOP-SAF-01).
3. Use the overhead crane (certified operator, cert CRANE) and the die cart; verify die weight vs crane rating. Follow lift plan.
4. Install the new die, connect cooling circuits, pressure-test the circuits at working pressure for 5 minutes, and verify zero leak before heating.
5. Run the die warm-up and first-off qualification.

title: Die Change and Die Cooling Leak / Molten Metal Safety
text:
[SOP-CAS-02: Die Change and Die Cooling Leak / Molten Metal Safety]
## Die cooling leak (GP-DIE-LEAK) - Level 6 notification
Water entering a molten-aluminum cavity can cause a violent steam explosion. If a leak is suspected (steam, popping, water at parting line, moisture on casting): stop the cycle, clear the area by 10 m, do not open the press until the die surface temperature and cooling circuits have been checked, notify the Casting Area Manager and EHS, and pull the die under SOP-CAS-02 with the Maintenance Manager's approval.

title: Die Change and Die Cooling Leak / Molten Metal Safety
text:
[SOP-CAS-02: Die Change and Die Cooling Leak / Molten Metal Safety]
## Molten metal PPE
Aluminized coat and hood, face shield, heat-resistant gloves, safety boots with metatarsal protection. No wet tools or moist alloy ingots near the furnace.

title: Shot Sleeve and Plunger Tip Inspection
text:
[SOP-CAS-03: Shot Sleeve and Plunger Tip Inspection]
**Area:** CAS  |  **Owner:** Reliability Engineer  |  **Revision:** B  |  **Effective:** 2025-06-01

> **Synthetic training document.** Written for the Voltara Motors digital-twin demo. It is modeled on public OEM and industry information but it is NOT an OEM document. Inspect the plunger tip and shot sleeve every 400 operating hours or after any GP-SHOT-SLOW event.
- Measure plunger tip outside diameter and sleeve inside diameter; replace the tip when clearance exceeds the OEM limit or when scoring is visible.
- Check lubricant spray quality and plunger lubrication; check for aluminum buildup.
- Verify shot speed profile after replacement; record the first 20 shots.
- A worn tip raises fill time variation, increases porosity and can show as lower accumulator pressure drop.
Typical downtime for a planned tip change is 2-3 hours; unplanned replacement 2-8 hours.

title: Hydraulic System Fault Response: Low Pressure, High Temperature, Leaks, Filter dP
text:
[SOP-HYD-01: Hydraulic System Fault Response: Low Pressure, High Temperature, Leaks, Filter dP]
## General
Hydraulic systems on presses, the Giga Press and trim press store energy in accumulators. Always depressurize and LOTO before opening any hose, fitting, filter or valve.

title: Hydraulic System Fault Response: Low Pressure, High Temperature, Leaks, Filter dP
text:
[SOP-HYD-01: Hydraulic System Fault Response: Low Pressure, High Temperature, Leaks, Filter dP]
## Low pressure
1. Confirm gauge vs transducer; check reservoir level and pump motor current.
2. Check accumulator nitrogen pre-charge (should be 60-70% of minimum operating pressure); recharge or replace bladder/piston seals.
3. Check pump delivery vs baseline and case-drain flow (a rising drain flow indicates pump wear).
4. Inspect valve block cartridges for internal leakage; swap in a known good cartridge if available.
5. Replace suction strainer if clogged; check oil viscosity.

title: Hydraulic System Fault Response: Low Pressure, High Temperature, Leaks, Filter dP
text:
[SOP-HYD-01: Hydraulic System Fault Response: Low Pressure, High Temperature, Leaks, Filter dP]
## High oil temperature
Check cooling water flow and inlet temperature, clean the cooler, verify the thermostatic valve, and trend temperature versus cycle count. A steady rise at constant load often indicates pump internal leakage (energy converting to heat).

title: Hydraulic System Fault Response: Low Pressure, High Temperature, Leaks, Filter dP
text:
[SOP-HYD-01: Hydraulic System Fault Response: Low Pressure, High Temperature, Leaks, Filter dP]
## Hose/fitting leaks
Isolate and depressurize per LOTO; replace hose with the same part number and date code, torque fitting to spec, clean up spills (SOP-ENV-01), top up reservoir with the correct oil grade; run and inspect under pressure from a safe distance.

title: Hydraulic System Fault Response: Low Pressure, High Temperature, Leaks, Filter dP
text:
[SOP-HYD-01: Hydraulic System Fault Response: Low Pressure, High Temperature, Leaks, Filter dP]
## Filters
Replace return and pressure filters at amber dP indicator or at the PM interval; take an oil sample if the filter loaded abnormally fast. Target cleanliness ISO 4406 17/15/12 or better for proportional/servo valves.

title: Hydraulic System Fault Response: Low Pressure, High Temperature, Leaks, Filter dP
text:
[SOP-HYD-01: Hydraulic System Fault Response: Low Pressure, High Temperature, Leaks, Filter dP]
## Escalation
Pressure or temperature in alarm, oil fire risk, or a leak larger than 5 gallons: page the Maintenance Supervisor and EHS.

[SOP-BAT-01: Pack Fastening, Torque Traceability and Isolated Tooling]
## Equipment
Synchronous four-spindle fastening stations (Desoutter) apply up to 20 Nm to fix the pack at four points simultaneously; the spindles are galvanically isolated to protect workers near HV busbars. Corded isolated angle drivers are used for busbar rework.

title: Pack Fastening, Torque Traceability and Isolated Tooling
text:
[SOP-BAT-01: Pack Fastening, Torque Traceability and Isolated Tooling]
## Procedure
1. Daily torque verification on the test joint (record in the daily check). Reject the station if the verification falls outside +/- 5%.
2. All tightening results are recorded against the VIN/pack serial. NOK results are not re-tightened without quality approval.
3. A **missed-bolt (TQ-BATCH-MISS)** event quarantines the pack, and requires re-inspection by a quality inspector before release.
4. Inspect isolation of chucks and cables at each PM; replace damaged cables (TQ-CBL-FAULT).
5. Transducer calibration yearly (or every 500k cycles); station without valid certificate must not run.

title: Pack Fastening, Torque Traceability and Isolated Tooling
text:
[SOP-BAT-01: Pack Fastening, Torque Traceability and Isolated Tooling]
## Typical torque faults
- TQ-NOK: out-of-window torque - check cross-threading, socket wear, transducer drift and fastener lot friction.
- TQ-MOTOR-TEMP: tool temperature rising - verify duty cycle, replace gear head if abnormal.

title: Laser Safety and Protective Glass Replacement
text:
[SOP-BAT-02: Laser Safety and Protective Glass Replacement]
**Area:** BAT  |  **Owner:** Process Engineer  |  **Revision:** B  |  **Effective:** 2025-06-01

Class 4 lasers (TruDisk disk lasers for busbar welding and laser brazing) require a Laser Safety Officer (cert LASER) for any enclosure access.
- Interlocks and shutter checks daily; fume extraction verified before use.
- **Protective cover glass** is the most common consumable: contamination leads to power loss (LSR-PWR-LOW). Replace when the measured power at the workpiece falls below 94% of nominal (alarm 90%) or when the cleaning cycle no longer restores power. Inspect glass at the start of each shift in BAT-BL cells (daily PM) and weekly in brazing cells.
- After replacing the glass, run a power measurement and a seam test; record readings.
- Chiller outlet temperature must stay within 20-25 C; above 27 C triggers inspection of chiller filters/condenser.
- Never defeat interlocks; the shutter must confirm open before beam on.

- Failed packs are quarantined, retested once, and sent to rework if still failing. Check seal/gasket, fastening torque history and glue bead record in MES.

text:
[SOP-BAT-03: Pack End-of-Line: Helium Leak Test and HV Test Fail Handling]
## HV / insulation / functional test
- Insulation resistance or functional failure: quarantine the pack in the marked area, inform the HV Safety Engineer if there is any voltage anomaly or swelling.
- False-fail trends (TST-FALSE-FAIL) are investigated for contact wear in the fixture (pogo pins) and threshold drift before touching packs.
- Packs that fail twice go to teardown with Quality; keep the data trace.

title: Torque NOK Handling and Tool Calibration (General Assembly)
text:
[SOP-QA-01: Torque NOK Handling and Tool Calibration (General Assembly)]
**Area:** GA  |  **Owner:** Quality Engineer  |  **Revision:** B  |  **Effective:** 2025-06-01

> **Synthetic training document.** Written for the Voltara Motors digital-twin demo. It is modeled on public OEM and industry information but it is NOT an OEM document. Items tagged `oem_public` were checked against public sources; items tagged `synthetic` are invented for realism. Do not use for real equipment.

- Atlas Copco Power Focus controllers log each tightening with VIN, torque, angle and status.
- NOK actions: stop the station, inspect fastener and joint, **do not re-tighten** without quality approval, and check the daily test joint verification.
- Three NOKs in a row, or 2% NOK rate in a shift, triggers a containment: check tool calibration, socket wear, and fastener batch; quarantine suspect lots; audit the last 20 vehicles.
- Calibration: transducer calibration every 12 months or 500k cycles; overdue tools are tagged out (TQ-CAL-DUE).
- Cable faults (TQ-CBL-FAULT) and tool overtemperature (TQ-MOTOR-TEMP) are handled by process technicians.

title: Containment and Quarantine of Suspect Vehicles/Parts
text:
[SOP-QA-02: Containment and Quarantine of Suspect Vehicles/Parts]
**Area:** ALL  |  **Owner:** Quality Manager  |  **Revision:** B  |  **Effective:** 2025-06-01

> **Synthetic training document.** Written for the Voltara Motors digital-twin demo. It is modeled on public OEM and industry information but it is NOT an OEM document. Items tagged `oem_public` were checked against public sources; items tagged `synthetic` are invented for realism. Do not use for real equipment.

1. Stop shipping affected units; apply a Quality hold tag in MES.
2. Identify scope using shift, machine, time window, and VIN range from the CMMS and MES.
3. Segregate parts physically in the red-tag area.
4. Perform 100% re-inspection until the root cause is fixed and 3 consecutive good lots verified.
5. Record disposition (rework, scrap, release) and customer-impact assessment.
Large downtime events with possible quality impact (e.g. weld parameter drift, paint film defect, laser power drop) always trigger containment for units made since the last verified good check.

title: Conveyor, AGV and AMR Fault Response
text:
[SOP-GA-01: Conveyor, AGV and AMR Fault Response]
**Area:** GA  |  **Owner:** General Assembly Area Manager  |  **Revision:** B  |  **Effective:** 2025-06-01

> **Synthetic training document.** Written for the Voltara Motors digital-twin demo. It is modeled on public OEM and industry information but it is NOT an OEM document. Items tagged `oem_public` were checked against public sources; items tagged `synthetic` are invented for realism. Do not use for real equipment.

- **Conveyor jam (CNV-JAM):** LOTO before clearing; check carrier alignment, photo-eye cleanliness and chain tension.
- **Drive overload (CNV-DRV-OVL):** check for mechanical resistance, motor current vs nameplate; replace gearmotor if abnormal; vibration above 5 mm/s is a warn.
- **Chain elongation:** measure elongation, replace the chain section above 3%.
- **AGV/AMR localization lost (AGV-NAV-LOST):** re-localize at a charging station; update map if layout changed.
- **Safety scanner fault (AGV-LIDAR):** clean lens, verify protective field with test object; never bypass.
- **Low battery or charge contact failure:** replace contact set; verify charger.
- Decking AGVs carrying battery packs: a stopped AGV in the marriage station blocks the line (criticality A). Notify the supervisor immediately.

title: Compressed Air System: Compressor Trip and Low Pressure Response
text:
[SOP-UTL-01: Compressed Air System: Compressor Trip and Low Pressure Response]
**Area:** UTL  |  **Owner:** Utilities Supervisor  |  **Revision:** B  |  **Effective:** 2025-06-01

> **Synthetic training document.** Written for the Voltara Motors digital-twin demo. It is modeled on public OEM and industry information but it is NOT an OEM document. Items tagged `oem_public` were checked against public sources; items tagged `synthetic` are invented for realism. Do not use for real equipment.

- Plant air header normal 7.5 bar; if pressure falls below 6.0 bar start the standby compressor and prepare to shed non-critical loads (blow-off, cleaning).
- **Discharge temperature high (CMP-DISCH-TEMP):** nominal ~85 C; warn 100 C; alarm 108 C. Check cooler fouling (Texas summer), oil level and thermostatic valve; clean cooler fins; check ambient ventilation.
- **Oil separator dP high:** replace separator element (typically at 0.9 bar differential).
- **Dryer dew point alarm:** check condensate drains; service dryer.
- **Motor overload trip:** check bearings and supply voltage imbalance.
- Run the lead/lag schedule weekly so run hours stay balanced across the four compressors.

title: Run-Extension and Run-to-Failure Risk Decision (e.g. 'Keep running 2 more hours?')
text:
[SOP-OPS-02: Run-Extension and Run-to-Failure Risk Decision (e.g. 'Keep running 2 more hours?')]
## Purpose
Provide a consistent, risk-based way to decide whether a machine showing warning signs may keep producing until a planned stop, a shift end, or a defined time extension.

title: Run-Extension and Run-to-Failure Risk Decision (e.g. 'Keep running 2 more hours?')
text:
[SOP-OPS-02: Run-Extension and Run-to-Failure Risk Decision (e.g. 'Keep running 2 more hours?')]
## Inputs to the decision
1. Machine criticality (A/B/C) and buffer status (how many minutes of downstream stock exist).
2. Sensor channels vs thresholds: nominal / warn / alarm, trend slope (rate of change per hour), and SHAP-contributing features from the anomaly alert.
3. Fault history: same fault code in the last 14/90 days; recent PdM work orders; days since last PM.
4. Safety potential: could the failure create a hazard (HV, molten metal, Ex-zone, hydraulic burst, crane load)?
5. Consequence: estimated downtime if it fails (MTTR for the fault code from the machine manual), parts availability, lost vehicles per hour.

title: Run-Extension and Run-to-Failure Risk Decision (e.g. 'Keep running 2 more hours?')
text:
[SOP-OPS-02: Run-Extension and Run-to-Failure Risk Decision (e.g. 'Keep running 2 more hours?')]
## Rules
- **Safety-critical channels at warn or worse:** never extend. Stop at the earliest safe point and notify L3/L4.
- **Any channel at alarm:** no extension unless the Maintenance Manager approves in writing with a mitigation (reduced speed, extra monitoring every 15 min, tech on standby).
- **Channel at warn, trend flat (< 2% change per hour):** extension up to 2 hours allowed with supervisor approval; technician inspects at the next break; re-evaluate every 30 minutes.
- **Channel at warn, trend rising (> 2% per hour or accelerating):** extension limited to the time needed to complete the current batch or reach a buffer-protected stop (max 30-60 min); schedule repair immediately.
- **Between 70% and 100% of nominal-to-warn distance:** extension allowed to the end of shift; raise PdM work order; add watch to handover.
- **Repeat failure (same fault within 14 days):** treat as warn at minimum; engineer must approve.
- **Criticality-A machine with no spare for a high-MTTR part:** do not run beyond the planned window unless production loss from stopping exceeds the expected loss from a failure (expected loss = probability of failure x MTTR x loss/hour). Document the calculation.

title: Run-Extension and Run-to-Failure Risk Decision (e.g. 'Keep running 2 more hours?')
text:
[SOP-OPS-02: Run-Extension and Run-to-Failure Risk Decision (e.g. 'Keep running 2 more hours?')]
## Documentation
Record the decision, approver, time limit, mitigations and monitoring in the work order and shift handover. After the extension, close the loop: confirm outcome and update the PdM/anomaly model feedback.

title: Roll & Brake Dynamometer and ADAS Calibration: Failure Handling
text:
[SOP-EOL-01: Roll & Brake Dynamometer and ADAS Calibration: Failure Handling]
**Area:** EOL  |  **Owner:** EOL Area Manager  |  **Revision:** B  |  **Effective:** 2025-06-01

> **Synthetic training document.** Written for the Voltara Motors digital-twin demo. It is modeled on public OEM and industry information but it is NOT an OEM document. Items tagged `oem_public` were checked against public sources; items tagged `synthetic` are invented for realism. Do not use for real equipment.

- Dynamometer: roller surface and bearing check weekly; calibration of speed/force sensors annually. A failed dyno test never releases the vehicle: re-run once after checking tire pressure, wheel-end torque and strap tension; second failure goes to diagnostic bay.
- ADAS calibration: target alignment verified monthly; vehicle must be on level floor and tire pressures set; out-of-window results (e.g. camera aim) require recalibration and recording; repeated failures on the same bay indicate target/alignment drift (check with reference vehicle).
- Test station communication loss to MES (TST-COMM) stops release; controls technician restarts service and checks network.

title: 5-Axis Machining Center: Spindle Vibration, Coolant, ATC and Dimensional Drift
text:
[SOP-CNC-01: 5-Axis Machining Center: Spindle Vibration, Coolant, ATC and Dimensional Drift]
**Area:** CAS  |  **Owner:** Casting Area Manager  |  **Revision:** B  |  **Effective:** 2025-06-01

> **Synthetic training document.** Written for the Voltara Motors digital-twin demo. It is modeled on public OEM and industry information but it is NOT an OEM document. Items tagged `oem_public` were checked against public sources; items tagged `synthetic` are invented for realism. Do not use for real equipment.

- Spindle vibration trending up (nominal ~1.2 mm/s; warn 4.0; alarm 6.5): check tool balance and drawbar clamp force first, then bearings; plan spindle exchange at alarm (a 3-12 hour job).
- Coolant: concentration 7-9% by refractometer; check weekly; replace filter bags at dP alarm.
- ATC faults: check air pressure (at least 6 bar), gripper wear and positions.
- Part dimension drift: run the warm-up program, re-qualify tool offsets, check fixture clamping pads; thermal growth is common after long idle periods.
- Ballscrew and linear scale faults: check lubrication; backlash measurement.

[Machine Manual: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 (Giga Press)]
## 1. Identification

- **Plant machine IDs:** CAS-GP-01, M01
- **Manufacturer / model:** IDRA / GIGAPRESS NEO 6100
- **Description:** High-pressure aluminum die casting machine, 6,100 t class (60,000 kN clamping force), die height 2,400 mm, ~430 t, 20.4 x 7.4 x 6.3 m. Produces the single-piece rear underbody casting.
- **Typical cycle time:** 95 s
- **Key specifications** (oem_public): clamping_force_kN = 60000, weight_t = 430

title: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 manual
text:
[Machine Manual: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 (Giga Press)]
## 2. Verified public reference facts

- IDRA publishes the GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 at 60,000 kN clamping force, 2,400 mm die height, ~430 t weight and 20.4 x 7.4 x 6.3 m footprint. (source: https://idragroup.com/sites/default/files/download/gigapress-catalogue-en_0.pdf)
- Features: DCP hydraulic system with integrated high-flow manifold blocks, Inject Computer 3.x machine management, cell controller integration, easy-maintenance all-in-one manifolds to minimise fluid loss. (source: https://idragroup.com/sites/default/files/download/gigapress-catalogue-en_0.pdf)
- A 6,000 t Giga Press achieves fill times around 120 milliseconds; platens were redesigned and cores moved externally to improve dimensional accuracy. (source: https://leandesign.com/?p=2932)
- IDRA NEO machines use Block-Control tie-bar monitoring with automatic clamping-force adjustment, automatic toggle lubrication and a servo-driven guarding system (per NEO 1000 listing). (source: https://www.werktuigen.com/idra-neo+1000/wt-223-58307)

[Machine Manual: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 (Giga Press)]
## 6. Fault code reference and troubleshooting

Severity: 1 minor, 2 moderate, 3 major, 4 critical (safety or long stop). MTTR = typical repair time range.

title: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 manual
text:
[Machine Manual: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 (Giga Press)]
### GP-PRESS-LOW: Hydraulic system pressure below setpoint
- **Severity:** 3  |  **Typical MTTR:** 60-360 min  |  **Trade:** Hydraulics / Pneumatics  |  **Code source:** `synthetic`
- **Probable causes:** Pump wear; Internal leakage in valve block; Accumulator pre-charge loss; Clogged suction strainer
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Check pump delivery and case drain flow
  2. Check accumulator nitrogen pre-charge
  3. Inspect suction strainer
  4. Replace worn pump or valve cartridge
- **Parts likely needed:** HYD-CART-VLV (Proportional valve cartridge); HYD-FLT-10M (10 micron return filter)
- **Early-warning signature:** channel `hyd_pressure_bar` shows drift down before failure.
- **Escalation:** page the Maintenance Supervisor at once for severity 3+ faults.

title: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 manual
text:
[Machine Manual: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 (Giga Press)]
### GP-TEMP-HIGH: Hydraulic oil temperature high
- **Severity:** 2  |  **Typical MTTR:** 30-180 min  |  **Trade:** Hydraulics / Pneumatics  |  **Code source:** `synthetic`
- **Probable causes:** Cooler fouled; Cooling water flow low; Pump internal leakage
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Clean oil cooler, verify water flow
  2. Check thermostat valve
  3. Trend temperature vs. cycle count
- **Parts likely needed:** HYD-COOLER-PLATE (Plate-type oil cooler cleaning kit)
- **Early-warning signature:** channel `hyd_temp_c` shows drift up before failure.

title: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 manual
text:
[Machine Manual: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 (Giga Press)]
### GP-LEAK: Hydraulic oil leak at hose / fitting
- **Severity:** 2  |  **Typical MTTR:** 45-240 min  |  **Trade:** Hydraulics / Pneumatics  |  **Code source:** `synthetic`
- **Probable causes:** Hose abrasion; Fitting loosened by vibration; Seal failure
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Isolate and depressurize per LOTO
  2. Replace hose/fitting, torque to spec
  3. Clean up and top up reservoir
- **Parts likely needed:** HYD-HOSE-ASM (High-pressure hose assembly)
- **Early-warning signature:** channel `hyd_level_pct` shows drift down before failure.

title: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 manual
text:
[Machine Manual: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 (Giga Press)]
### GP-FILTER-DP: Filter differential pressure high
- **Severity:** 1  |  **Typical MTTR:** 20-60 min  |  **Trade:** Hydraulics / Pneumatics  |  **Code source:** `synthetic`
- **Probable causes:** Filter loaded with particles
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Replace pressure and return filters
  2. Sample oil for particle count (ISO 4406)
- **Parts likely needed:** HYD-FLT-10M (10 micron return filter)
- **Early-warning signature:** channel `hyd_filter_dp_bar` shows drift up before failure.

title: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 manual
text:
[Machine Manual: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 (Giga Press)]
### GP-VALVE-STICK: Servo/proportional valve sticking - position deviation
- **Severity:** 3  |  **Typical MTTR:** 90-420 min  |  **Trade:** Hydraulics / Pneumatics  |  **Code source:** `synthetic`
- **Probable causes:** Contaminated oil; Valve spool wear; Amplifier drift
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Flush and filter oil
  2. Replace valve; run valve calibration
- **Parts likely needed:** HYD-VLV-SERVO (Servo valve)
- **Early-warning signature:** channel `vibration_mm_s` shows spike before failure.
- **Escalation:** page the Maintenance Supervisor at once for severity 3+ faults.

title: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 manual
text:
[Machine Manual: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 (Giga Press)]
### GP-TIEBAR: Tie-bar load imbalance: clamping force deviation across 4 tie bars
- **Severity:** 3  |  **Typical MTTR:** 90-360 min  |  **Trade:** Mechanical  |  **Code source:** `synthetic`
- **Probable causes:** Die thermal growth; Toggle lubrication lack; Sensor drift
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Run Block-Control tie-bar calibration
  2. Check automatic toggle lubrication
  3. Re-level die
- **Parts likely needed:** GP-TIEBAR-SNSR (Tie-bar strain sensor)
- **Early-warning signature:** channel `vibration_mm_s` shows drift up before failure.
- **Escalation:** page the Maintenance Supervisor at once for severity 3+ faults.

title: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 manual
text:
[Machine Manual: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 (Giga Press)]
### GP-SHOT-SLOW: Shot speed profile deviation / fill time out of window (~120 ms target)
- **Severity:** 3  |  **Typical MTTR:** 120-480 min  |  **Trade:** Hydraulics / Pneumatics  |  **Code source:** `synthetic`
- **Probable causes:** Accumulator pre-charge low; Shot sleeve wear; Valve response degraded
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Check accumulator pre-charge
  2. Inspect shot sleeve and plunger tip
  3. Calibrate injection valve
- **Parts likely needed:** GP-PLUNGER-TIP (Plunger tip)
- **Early-warning signature:** channel `hyd_pressure_bar` shows drift down before failure.
- **Escalation:** page the Maintenance Supervisor at once for severity 3+ faults.

title: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 manual
text:
[Machine Manual: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 (Giga Press)]
### GP-DIE-LEAK: Die cooling circuit water leak into die cavity
- **Severity:** 4  |  **Typical MTTR:** 240-1200 min  |  **Trade:** Mechanical  |  **Code source:** `synthetic`
- **Probable causes:** Cracked cooling insert; O-ring failure
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Stop cycle and secure die; pull die per SOP-CAS-02
  2. Pressure test circuits; replace insert
- **Parts likely needed:** GP-ORING-KIT (Die cooling O-ring kit)

title: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 manual
text:

### GP-GUARD-SERVO: Servo guard door fault / interlock

title: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 manual
text:
[Machine Manual: IDRA GIGAPRESS NEO 6100 (Giga Press)]
## 7. Symptom-to-cause quick guide

- If `hyd_pressure_bar` is abnormal, think of: GP-PRESS-LOW (hydraulic system pressure below setpoint); GP-SHOT-SLOW (shot speed profile deviation / fill time out of window (~120 ms target)).
- If `hyd_temp_c` is abnormal, think of: GP-TEMP-HIGH (hydraulic oil temperature high).
- If `hyd_level_pct` is abnormal, think of: GP-LEAK (hydraulic oil leak at hose / fitting).
- If `hyd_filter_dp_bar` is abnormal, think of: GP-FILTER-DP (filter differential pressure high).
- If `vibration_mm_s` is abnormal, think of: GP-VALVE-STICK (servo/proportional valve sticking - position deviation); GP-TIEBAR (tie-bar load imbalance: clamping force deviation across 4 tie bars).
- If the machine stops with no code: check E-stop chain/safety devices, air/water supply, and PLC/MES communication.
- Repeated faults within 14 days: escalate to the area engineer (see SOP-MNT-01) and review the work order history.

- Typical battery: A02B-0200-K102 lithium (robot base); clear with RES_PCA then master. (source: https://industrialmonitordirect.com/blogs/knowledgebase/fanuc-srvo-062-bzal-alarm-mastering-recovery-procedure)
- SRVO-050 collision detect, SRVO-007 external emergency stop, SRVO-402 DCS alarm and SRVO-230/231 chain abnormal are among frequently encountered FANUC alarms. (source: https://acieta.com/video-library/service)
- OEM PM guidance quoted by CMMS vendors: grease replenishment for J4-J6 at about 600 hrs; full PM (gearbox oil/grease) about 3,850 hrs or 12 months. (source: https://oxmaint.com/industries/steel-plant/industrial-robotic-arm-maintenance-steel-plants-fanuc-kuka-abb)

[Machine Manual: FANUC M-900iB/360 (Blank Handling Robot)]
### SRVO-062: BZAL alarm: pulsecoder backup battery voltage zero, absolute position lost
- **Severity:** 3  |  **Typical MTTR:** 90-300 min  |  **Trade:** Robotics  |  **Code source:** `oem_public`
- **Probable causes:** Encoder backup battery fully discharged; Battery cable disconnected or broken inside base; Controller powered off for a long period with dead battery
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Replace robot base and controller batteries (A02B-0200-K102 lithium)
  2. Clear alarm with RES_PCA from the pulsecoder screen and cycle power
  3. Re-master the affected axes (zero-position or quick mastering) and verify against witness marks
  4. Validate TCP and run the weld/path accuracy check before returning to production
- **Parts likely needed:** FAN-A02B-0200-K102 (Lithium backup battery A02B-0200-K102)
- **Early-warning signature:** channel `battery_voltage_v` shows decay before failure.
- **Escalation:** page the Maintenance Supervisor at once for severity 3+ faults.

title: FANUC M-900iB/360 manual
text:

### SRVO-065: BLAL alarm: pulsecoder battery voltage low (data still intact)
- **Severity:** 1  |  **Typical MTTR:** 20-45 min  |  **Trade:** Robotics  |  **Code source:** `oem_public`
- **Probable causes:** Battery approaching end of life (1-2 year typical life); Missed preventive battery replacement
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Replace batteries within the same shift while power is ON to keep mastering data
  2. Record replacement date on the robot asset tag
- **Parts likely needed:** FAN-A02B-0200-K102 (Lithium backup battery A02B-0200-K102)
- **Early-warning signature:** channel `battery_voltage_v` shows decay before failure.

### SRVO-050: Collision detect alarm
- **Severity:** 2  |  **Typical MTTR:** 15-120 min  |  **Trade:** Robotics  |  **Code source:** `oem_public`
- **Probable causes:** Part or fixture misplaced in the cell; Gun tip stuck to panel; Wrong payload setting; Reducer wear causing disturbance torque rise
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Back the robot out in T1 using the collision release
  2. Inspect tooling, gun and fixture for damage
  3. Verify payload/armload settings
  4. Check J2/J3 reducer for abnormal noise and disturbance torque

## 7. Symptom-to-cause quick guide

- If `battery_voltage_v` is abnormal, think of: SRVO-062 (bZAL alarm: pulsecoder backup battery voltage zero, absolute position lost); SRVO-065 (bLAL alarm: pulsecoder battery voltage low (data still intact)).
- If `motor_current_a` is abnormal, think of: SRVO-050 (collision detect alarm).
- If `motor_temp_c` is abnormal, think of: SRVO-021 (sRDY off: servo amplifier not ready).
- If the machine stops with no code: check E-stop chain/safety devices, air/water supply, and PLC/MES communication.
- Repeated faults within 14 days: escalate to the area engineer (see SOP-MNT-01) and review the work order history.

[Machine Manual: FANUC R-2000iC/210F (Spot Weld Robot (FANUC))]
### SRVO-062: BZAL alarm: pulsecoder backup battery voltage zero, absolute position lost
- **Severity:** 3  |  **Typical MTTR:** 90-300 min  |  **Trade:** Robotics  |  **Code source:** `oem_public`
- **Probable causes:** Encoder backup battery fully discharged; Battery cable disconnected or broken inside base; Controller powered off for a long period with dead battery
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Replace robot base and controller batteries (A02B-0200-K102 lithium)
  2. Clear alarm with RES_PCA from the pulsecoder screen and cycle power
  3. Re-master the affected axes (zero-position or quick mastering) and verify against witness marks
  4. Validate TCP and run the weld/path accuracy check before returning to production
- **Parts likely needed:** FAN-A02B-0200-K102 (Lithium backup battery A02B-0200-K102)
- **Early-warning signature:** channel `battery_voltage_v` shows decay before failure.
- **Escalation:** page the Maintenance Supervisor at once for severity 3+ faults.

text:

- **Severity:** 1  |  **Typical MTTR:** 20-45 min  |  **Trade:** Robotics  |  **Code source:** `oem_public`
- **Probable causes:** Battery approaching end of life (1-2 year typical life); Missed preventive battery replacement
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Replace batteries within the same shift while power is ON to keep mastering data
  2. Record replacement date on the robot asset tag
- **Parts likely needed:** FAN-A02B-0200-K102 (Lithium backup battery A02B-0200-K102)
- **Early-warning signature:** channel `battery_voltage_v` shows decay before failure.

## 2. Verified public reference facts

- SRVO-062 BZAL: no backup battery voltage detected at the pulsecoder - mastering data lost, remastering required; SRVO-065 BLAL: low battery voltage warning, data still intact. Typical battery life 1-2 years. (source: https://industrialmonitordirect.com/blogs/knowledgebase/fanuc-srvo-062-bzal-alarm-troubleshooting-resolution)

- OEM PM guidance quoted by CMMS vendors: grease replenishment for J4-J6 at about 600 hrs; full PM (gearbox oil/grease) about 3,850 hrs or 12 months. (source: https://oxmaint.com/industries/steel-plant/industrial-robotic-arm-maintenance-steel-plants-fanuc-kuka-abb)

title: FANUC M-10iD/12 manual
text:
[Machine Manual: FANUC M-10iD/12 (Cell Stacking Robot)]
### SRVO-062: BZAL alarm: pulsecoder backup battery voltage zero, absolute position lost
- **Severity:** 3  |  **Typical MTTR:** 90-300 min  |  **Trade:** Robotics  |  **Code source:** `oem_public`
- **Probable causes:** Encoder backup battery fully discharged; Battery cable disconnected or broken inside base; Controller powered off for a long period with dead battery
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Replace robot base and controller batteries (A02B-0200-K102 lithium)
  2. Clear alarm with RES_PCA from the pulsecoder screen and cycle power
  3. Re-master the affected axes (zero-position or quick mastering) and verify against witness marks
  4. Validate TCP and run the weld/path accuracy check before returning to production
- **Parts likely needed:** FAN-A02B-0200-K102 (Lithium backup battery A02B-0200-K102)
- **Early-warning signature:** channel `battery_voltage_v` shows decay before failure.
- **Escalation:** page the Maintenance Supervisor at once for severity 3+ faults.

title: FANUC M-10iD/12 manual
text:
[Machine Manual: FANUC M-10iD/12 (Cell Stacking Robot)]
### SRVO-065: BLAL alarm: pulsecoder battery voltage low (data still intact)
- **Severity:** 1  |  **Typical MTTR:** 20-45 min  |  **Trade:** Robotics  |  **Code source:** `oem_public`
- **Probable causes:** Battery approaching end of life (1-2 year typical life); Missed preventive battery replacement
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Replace batteries within the same shift while power is ON to keep mastering data
  2. Record replacement date on the robot asset tag
- **Parts likely needed:** FAN-A02B-0200-K102 (Lithium backup battery A02B-0200-K102)
- **Early-warning signature:** channel `battery_voltage_v` shows decay before failure.

title: FANUC M-10iD/12 manual
text:
[Machine Manual: FANUC M-10iD/12 (Cell Stacking Robot)]
### SRVO-050: Collision detect alarm
- **Severity:** 2  |  **Typical MTTR:** 15-120 min  |  **Trade:** Robotics  |  **Code source:** `oem_public`
- **Probable causes:** Part or fixture misplaced in the cell; Gun tip stuck to panel; Wrong payload setting; Reducer wear causing disturbance torque rise
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Back the robot out in T1 using the collision release
  2. Inspect tooling, gun and fixture for damage
  3. Verify payload/armload settings
  4. Check J2/J3 reducer for abnormal noise and disturbance torque
- **Early-warning signature:** channel `motor_current_a` shows spike before failure.

title: FANUC M-10iD/12 manual
text:

### SRVO-007: External emergency stop
- **Severity:** 2  |  **Typical MTTR:** 5-60 min  |  **Trade:** Robotics  |  **Code source:** `oem_public`
- **Probable causes:** Safety gate or light curtain tripped; E-stop button engaged; Safety relay fault
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Identify which safety device opened using the cell safety HMI
  2. Reset the device and the safety relay
  3. Verify chain status before resuming
- **Parts likely needed:** SAF-PILZ-PNOZ-S4 (Pilz PNOZ s4 safety relay)

- **Severity:** 3  |  **Typical MTTR:** 60-240 min  |  **Trade:** Robotics  |  **Code source:** `oem_public`
- **Probable causes:** DCS parameter checksum mismatch after a program change; Robot left safe zone; Mastering offset out of tolerance
- **Corrective actions:**
  1. Review DCS settings against the last approved backup
  2. Re-apply DCS parameters and cycle power
  3. Re-verify mastering; run DCS verification report and obtain controls engineer signoff
- **Escalation:** page the Maintenance Supervisor at once for severity 3+ faults.

  3. Replace socket if worn

title: SOP-MNT-M05-01: Weld robot axis 1 joint bearing wear: diagnosis and replacement
text:
[SOP-MNT-M05-01: Weld robot axis 1 joint bearing wear: diagnosis and replacement]
# SOP-MNT-M05-01: Weld robot axis 1 joint bearing wear: diagnosis and replacement

**Area:** BIW (twin station S06)  |  **Machine:** M05 Weld robot 2  |  **Owner:** Maintenance Supervisor  |  **Revision:** A  |  **Effective:** 2026-10-01

> **Synthetic training document** for the Voltara/Voltline digital-twin demo. Values tagged `synthetic` are invented. Not an OEM document.

title: SOP-MNT-M05-01: Symptom pattern
text:
[SOP-MNT-M05-01: Symptom pattern]
## Symptom pattern
- `vibration_rms` rises steadily over hours, with energy in the bearing defect band growing faster than overall RMS.
- `temperature_c` (axis 1 housing) climbs 10 to 15 C above baseline; `motor_current_a` rises about 10 to 15 percent under the same weld cycle.
- Cycle time slips and weld position quality can degrade as play grows.

title: SOP-MNT-M05-01: Likely cause (failure mode: bearing_wear)
text:
[SOP-MNT-M05-01: Likely cause (failure mode: bearing_wear)]
## Likely cause (failure mode: bearing_wear)
Lubricant breakdown or contamination at the axis 1 joint bearing (`m05_joint1_bearing`), often after a collision event or a missed regrease interval. Left running, wear accelerates and can seize the joint (long unplanned stop).

title: SOP-MNT-M05-01: Decision: keep running?
text:
[SOP-MNT-M05-01: Decision: keep running?]
## Decision: keep running?
Apply SOP-OPS-02. For M05 (criticality A) with vibration above 2x baseline and a rising trend, do not extend beyond the current batch. Plan the bearing change at the next buffer-protected stop.

title: SOP-MNT-M05-01: Replacement procedure (synthetic)
text:
[SOP-MNT-M05-01: Replacement procedure (synthetic)]
## Replacement procedure (synthetic)
1. Notify line lead and maintenance bay (S10). Raise a corrective work order for `m05_joint1_bearing`.
2. Pick spare part `bearing_6208` (Deep groove ball bearing 6208, A1 joint) from the spare parts cage (S12). Confirm stock and bin.
3. Lockout/tagout per SOP-SAF-01. Move robot to the service pose and support the arm.
4. Remove axis 1 cover, inspect for metal particles and contamination, take a photo for the work order.
5. Press out the worn bearing, clean the seat, fit the new bearing, regrease with the specified grease.
6. Reassemble, remove LOTO, run a dry cycle, then weld cycles at reduced speed for 10 cycles.
7. Confirm vibration and current back within 10 percent of baseline; close the work order and note the bearing hours.

title: SOP-MNT-M05-01: Time and parts (synthetic)
text:
[SOP-MNT-M05-01: Time and parts (synthetic)]
## Time and parts (synthetic)
- Typical repair time: 90 to 150 minutes (planned) once the part is at the machine.
- Crew: 1 technician plus 1 assistant. Spare stock: 2 on hand, lead time 9 days.

title: SOP-MNT-M05-01: Escalation
text:
[SOP-MNT-M05-01: Escalation]
## Escalation
Follow the M05 on-shift chain in the escalation matrix (L1 primary tech, L2 backup, L3 maintenance supervisor).

title: Past bearing seizure on Weld robot 1
text: Past incident (synthetic): on M04 Weld robot 1, axis 1 joint bearing vibration trended up over two shifts. The robot was run on for 3 hours past the first alert; the bearing seized and the line stopped for 4h 20m while the bearing was changed. Lesson: act on the first alert for bearing wear instead of extending the run. Reference SOP-OPS-02 and SOP-MNT-M05-01.

text: Failure modes the simulator can inject on M05 Weld robot 2 (station S06): bearing_wear on joint1_bearing: symptom high vibration, rising temperature; cause lubrication loss and fatigue; repair: Replace joint bearing and regrease (about 90 min, part bearing_6208) | bearing_wear on joint2_bearing: symptom high vibration, rising temperature; cause lubrication loss and fatigue; repair: Replace joint bearing and regrease (about 90 min, part bearing_6208) | servo_motor_fault on servo_motor: symptom high motor current, overheating; cause winding degradation; repair: Replace servo motor and recalibrate (about 150 min, part servo_motor_a) | gearbox_wear on gearbox: symptom noise, backlash; cause worn gear teeth; repair: Replace gearbox and retune (about 240 min, part gearbox_unit) | weld_tip_wear on weld_gun: symptom weak welds, quality alarms; cause electrode tip erosion; repair: Dress or replace electrode tips (about 20 min, part electrode_tips) | cable_harness_fatigue on cable_harness: symptom intermittent faults; cause flex fatigue; repair: Replace cable harness (about 75 min, part cable_harness_kit) | controller_fault on controller_cabinet: symptom controller error codes; cause I/O card failure; repair: Replace I/O card and reload program (about 60 min, part io_card)

title: Station S07 Inspection gate
text: Station S07 (Inspection gate): Camera arch checks weld quality and gaps. Machines: M07 Vision inspection gate. Receives from S06. Feeds S09. People: quality inspector.

title: Failure modes of M07 Vision inspection gate at S07
text: Failure modes the simulator can inject on M07 Vision inspection gate (station S07): camera_fault on camera: symptom no image; cause sensor failure; repair: Replace camera (about 60 min, part camera_unit) | lens_contamination on lens: symptom false rejects; cause dust and spatter; repair: Clean lens (about 10 min, part cleaning_kit) | calibration_drift on camera: symptom measurement drift; cause thermal drift; repair: Recalibrate (about 30 min, part none)

title: Station S08 Battery module line
text: Station S08 (Battery module line): Cells are stacked into modules. Machines: M08 Battery module stacker. Feeds S09.

title: Failure modes of M08 Battery module stacker at S08
text: Failure modes the simulator can inject on M08 Battery module stacker (station S08): belt_wear on drive_belt: symptom positioning error; cause wear; repair: Replace belt (about 60 min, part gantry_belt) | linear_guide_wear on linear_guide: symptom vibration; cause wear; repair: Replace guide block (about 120 min, part guide_block) | servo_motor_fault on servo_motor: symptom high current; cause winding fault; repair: Replace servo (about 120 min, part servo_motor_a)

title: Station S09 Pack closing and EOL test
text: Station S09 (Pack closing and EOL test): Pack is sealed, leak/electrical tested. Machines: M09 Pack sealer. Receives from S07, S08.

title: Failure modes of M09 Pack sealer at S09
text: Failure modes the simulator can inject on M09 Pack sealer (station S09): seal_head_wear on seal_head: symptom poor seals, leaks; cause wear; repair: Replace seal head (about 90 min, part seal_head) | heater_fault on heater: symptom low temperature; cause element burnout; repair: Replace heater (about 60 min, part heater_element) | leak_tester_fault on leak_tester: symptom false failures; cause sensor drift; repair: Recalibrate or replace sensor (about 45 min, part pressure_sensor)
